newsitem.title: USA: Gas leak forces evacuation of Texas prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Gas leak forces evacuation of Texas prisoners.

text.p: Nearly 4,000 prisoners were evacuated from a state prison complex on Monday to escape a billowing cloud of highly flammable gas leaking from a pipeline near Dayton, Texas.
The prisoners were transported by bus to jails in nearby towns because of the fear of an explosion, officials said.

A spokesman for pipeline operator Chevron Corp. said the line was filled with liquified petroleum gas, which turned into vapor when it vented into the atmosphere. Fire crews shot a steady stream of water on to the leak to reduce the possibility of ignition.
The leak occurred during work on a pipeline valve and could not be repaired until the gas had all leaked out, which was most likely to happen by sometime on Tuesday, the spokesman said.

Jail officials said at least five prisoners and a guard needed treatment at a hospital because of breathing problems when the gas began to fill the air around the prison, about half a mile from the leak.
Part of the complex houses female prisoners, some of whom were pregnant and were sent to other jails soon after the leak started.
Texas Department of Public Safety trooper Richard Vasser said there few residences in the area, so no further evacutions had been ordered.
"If we did have an explosion...they (residents) would know it, but I don't think it would do any damage," he told reporters.
Dayton is about 35 miles northeast of Houston.
